reply: {"title":"Leahy Law Waiver for Colombia","setting":"Colombia, 1998, U.S. executive branch.","decider":"The President","agent_recast":false,"recast_note":"","agent":"The President","agent_role":"decide","situation":"U.S. funding was barred for foreign military units with credible evidence of gross human-rights violations, subject to specified waiver conditions. The military situation in Colombia worsened during 1998 as the insurgent threat intensified.","question":"What should the President do about granting a national-security waiver from Leahy Law aid restrictions for Colombia in 1998?","facts":[{"id":"F1","kind":"authority","status":"confirmed","fact":"The Leahy Laws barred U.S. funding for a foreign military unit when credible evidence showed that the unit had committed gross violations of human rights.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p31.3"]},{"id":"F2","kind":"authority","status":"confirmed","fact":"The statutory provisions allowed waivers if the local government was acting to bring perpetrators to justice or vital U.S. national-security interests were at stake.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p31.3"]},{"id":"F3","kind":"situation","status":"confirmed","fact":"The Department of State used the Leahy Laws to withhold substantial aid from the Colombian Army.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p31.3"]},{"id":"F4","kind":"situation","status":"confirmed","fact":"No waivers under the Leahy Laws were initially granted for Colombia.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p31.3"]},{"id":"F5","kind":"situation","status":"confirmed","fact":"The Colombian Army’s top leadership objected to the Leahy Laws and, for a time, refused American assistance; many Colombian officers considered the laws and vetting procedures unjust and insulting to national honor.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p31.3"]},{"id":"F6","kind":"situation","status":"assessed","fact":"Some senior American officials sympathized with the Colombian military’s objections and believed the laws reflected unrealistic expectations among U.S. members of Congress.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p32.2"]},{"id":"F7","kind":"situation","status":"assessed","fact":"A senior State Department official argued that transforming military and police forces to meet human-rights and civil-liberties norms was exceptionally difficult while they faced hostile forces that disregarded those constraints.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p32.2"]},{"id":"F8","kind":"situation","status":"confirmed","fact":"The military situation in Colombia worsened dramatically in 1998.","spans":["src:9ddec1a6bcea#p32.2"]}],"options":{"O1":{"do":"The President grants Colombia a national-security waiver under the Leahy Laws.","move":"act","disposition":"grant","irreversible":false},"O2":{"do":"The President denies Colombia a national-security waiver under the Leahy Laws.","move":"act","disposition":"deny","irreversible":false}},"opposite_pair":["O1","O2"],"real_option":"O1","authored_options":["O2"],"no_opposite_reason":"","basis_statement":"The President’s stated rationale was that supporting Colombia was vital to U.S. national security."}
